candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Referrals/Case Management/Interprofessional Care: coordinate complex evaluations and referrals, collaborate with interdisciplinary teams, assess psychosocial/support needs, and facilitate continuity for clients requiring specialized care.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary coordination of heart-transplant candidate evaluation
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize heart-transplant candidacy evaluation as a multidisciplinary process that includes medical assessment plus psychosocial, behavioral, adherence, and support-system factors relevant to safe long-term transplant care.

options.A: It is a multidisciplinary assessment that integrates medical factors with psychosocial, behavioral, adherence, and support-system considerations relevant to transplant candidacy and post-transplant care.
options.B: It consists primarily of one cardiac imaging visit because psychosocial and support factors are assessed only after transplantation.
options.C: It evaluates medical eligibility alone because social support, adherence, substance use, and psychological factors are unrelated to transplant planning.
options.D: It has no structured or guideline-based domains, so each center evaluates candidates without reference to recognized transplant standards.

candidate.rationale: The current 2024 ISHLT guideline for cardiac-transplant candidates integrates numerous variables in patient selection and care, and current ISHLT psychosocial recommendations identify psychosocial evaluation as an integral part of transplant candidacy and care planning. Evaluation is therefore multidisciplinary rather than medical-only and includes factors that affect the client's ability to safely undergo and manage transplantation. B and C incorrectly exclude psychosocial/support domains, and D ignores current ISHLT guideline frameworks.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports comprehensive multidisciplinary cardiac-transplant candidate evaluation and inclusion of psychosocial/support factors as integral to selection and care planning.
candidate.source_document_title: ISHLT Guidelines for the Evaluation and Care of Cardiac Transplant Candidates; ISHLT/APM/AST/ICCAC/STSW Recommendations for the Psychosocial Evaluation of Adult Cardiothoracic Transplant Candidates
candidate.source_locator: 2024 ISHLT candidate-guideline overview: integrates numerous variables involved in evaluating patients for transplantation and updates patient-selection criteria and collaborative candidate care. 2018 adult psychosocial recommendations → introductory rationale: transplant/MCS candidates undergo a multifaceted assessment; psychosocial evaluation is integral for patient selection, care planning, interventions, referrals, and post-transplant/post-implant care; recommendations define content/process for comprehensive psychosocial evaluation.
candidate.source_organization: International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT)
candidate.source_version_date: Cardiac-candidate guideline published 2024-08-08; psychosocial recommendations published 2018-04-27
